intake.browser_storage: opt-in workspace only, and never a raw file or a cell value
retained_from_a_file: aggregate totals per day, org unit, and model
never_retained: any cell value, including in an error message
prompt, completion, or any free-text column

accepted_formats.label: Delimited text with a declared delimiter
Wawalu v1 provider-usage or HRIS-org JSON envelope

unsupported_containers.label: ZIP archive
unsupported_containers.why: Several consoles deliver the export as an archive; this page reads one text file at a time.
unsupported_containers.do_instead: Open the archive on your own machine and choose the CSV member named by the package below.

unsupported_containers.label: Compressed file
unsupported_containers.why: A compressed export is not decompressed here; nothing is written to disk by this page.
unsupported_containers.do_instead: Decompress it on your own machine, then choose the CSV inside it.

unsupported_containers.label: Spreadsheet workbook
unsupported_containers.why: A workbook carries formatting, formulas, and sheets this contract does not declare.
unsupported_containers.do_instead: Save the usage sheet as CSV, then choose that file.

unsupported_containers.label: Rendered invoice or report
unsupported_containers.why: An invoice is a picture of a total, not the daily rows the analysis needs.
unsupported_containers.do_instead: Request the usage or cost export instead of the invoice; the packages below name where.

unsupported_containers.label: Undeclared record format
unsupported_containers.why: This contract declares CSV, TSV, delimited text, and the v1 JSON envelope, and nothing else.
unsupported_containers.do_instead: Re-export as CSV, or convert it yourself before choosing the file.

export_request.requested_by: an organization owner or billing member
export_request.console_path: Settings → Organization → Usage, then Export for one billing period
export_request.ask_for: the cost and usage export, grouped by project and model
export_request.not: the invoice PDF, and not a per-user activity report

archive.lands_in: your own download folder — this page never looks there; you choose the file
archive.expected_content: one row per day, project, and model, with a cost column

before_import: Do not request the per-user breakdown; department-level rows are what the analysis reads.
Delete any column naming an individual account before you choose the file.

export_request.requested_by: a workspace admin or billing contact
export_request.console_path: Console → Usage, filtered to one period, then Export CSV
export_request.ask_for: usage and cost by workspace and model
export_request.not: the conversation or audit export, which carries prompt text and has its own contract

archive.lands_in: your own download folder; nothing is fetched from the console by this page
archive.expected_content: one row per day, workspace, and model, with input and output token columns

before_import: Export usage, not conversations; a conversation export is read under the never-render rule instead.
Remove any API-key label column — a key name identifies a person on small teams.

packages.label: AWS Cost and Usage Report (Bedrock lines)

export_request.requested_by: the payer-account owner or a FinOps engineer with Cost Explorer access
export_request.console_path: Billing → Data Exports → Standard data export, scoped to the Bedrock product code
export_request.ask_for: daily granularity with the cost-allocation tag that carries your cost centre
export_request.not: the full unfiltered CUR for every service, which is large and mostly irrelevant here

archive.delivery: written to an S3 bucket you own
archive.lands_in: your bucket; download one period yourself and choose that file
archive.member: the CSV part file inside the report folder for the period
archive.expected_content: line items with usage start date, unblended cost, and your cost-centre tag column

before_import: Decompress and, if the report is split into parts, choose one part per import.
Drop resource-id and account-id columns; the cost-centre tag is the only grouping this reads.

packages.label: Google Cloud billing export (Vertex AI lines)

export_request.console_path: Billing → Cost table, filtered to the Vertex AI service, then Download CSV
export_request.ask_for: daily cost by project and SKU for one month
export_request.not: the BigQuery detailed export, which carries far more than this contract declares

archive.lands_in: your own download folder; the billing account is never contacted from this page
archive.expected_content: one row per day, project, and SKU, with a cost column in the billing currency

before_import: Export one billing currency at a time; rows in a second currency are quarantined, not converted.
Remove label columns that carry a person's name or address.

packages.support: columns recognized; no normalizer shape yet, so this package reaches the manual column-mapping step

packages.label: Azure Cost Management export (Azure OpenAI lines)

export_request.requested_by: a subscription owner or cost-management contributor
export_request.console_path: Cost Management → Exports → new daily export, scoped to the Azure OpenAI service
export_request.ask_for: actual cost, daily, with the tag that carries your cost centre
export_request.not: amortized and actual in one file; pick one basis and stay on it across periods

archive.delivery: written to a storage account you own
archive.lands_in: your storage container; download one period yourself and choose that file
archive.container: single file per period, sometimes zipped
archive.member: the CSV for the period, if the download is an archive
archive.expected_content: one row per day, resource, and meter, with a cost column and your tag column

before_import: Keep one cost basis per import; mixing actual and amortized rows double-counts a period.
Drop resource-id and subscription-id columns before choosing the file.

packages.support: columns recognized; no normalizer shape yet, so this package reaches the manual column-mapping step

export_request.requested_by: an HRIS administrator or the people-operations partner who owns the org tree
export_request.console_path: your HRIS reporting section: a unit report, not a worker report
export_request.ask_for: unit id, parent unit, unit type, and whether the unit is active
export_request.not: a worker list — no person-level row is needed, accepted, or read

archive.delivery: downloads in your browser, or arrives from your HRIS partner
archive.lands_in: wherever you saved it; you choose it alongside the provider period
archive.expected_content: one row per organizational unit, with its parent

before_import: Send units, never people: delete name, email, title, manager, compensation, and location columns.
A unit smaller than the declared minimum group size is still a unit here; it is suppressed downstream.

unsupported_package.headline: This file is not one of the declared packages.
unsupported_package.recovery: Choose a .csv/.tsv provider usage export or org roster, or a .json v1 envelope. If your console delivered an archive, open it and choose the CSV inside.
unsupported_package.behaviour: The file is refused before it is parsed. Nothing about it is read, kept, or reported beyond its extension and media type.
unsupported_package.never: An unrecognized package is never partially parsed to see what it might have been.

partial.situation: Some rows are unreadable — a bad date, a negative amount, a short row.
partial.behaviour: The readable rows import and every rejected row is reported with a code, a row number, and a column name. Partial success is the normal case, not a failure.
partial.never: A rejected row is never silently dropped and never repaired by guessing.

stale.situation: The chosen file is an older period, or one already imported.
stale.behaviour: It imports. A delimited export carries no delivery sequence, so freshness is the reader's own file-picking decision; overlapping periods from one source reconcile by date, and the provenance label states the period that was read.
stale.never: A stale file never silently replaces a newer period's totals under a fresh-looking label.

malformed.situation: The file is not the shape it claims — an unclosed quoted field, a header with no data, a row count that disagrees with the header.
malformed.behaviour: The import is refused whole, with one code and one located coordinate. A ceiling breach (size or rows) is likewise a whole-file refusal, never a truncation.
malformed.never: No partial total is ever shown, because a short total is indistinguishable from a real one.

reordered.situation: Rows arrive out of date order, or periods are chosen in the wrong order.
reordered.behaviour: Accepted. Every aggregate is derived from the date column, so row order changes no figure, and multi-file selections are ordered by their declared periods rather than by pick order.
reordered.never: Row order is never treated as chronology.

duplicated.situation: The same period is chosen twice, or a file contains repeated rows.
duplicated.behaviour: Identical aggregate rows collapse; a repeated period from the same source is reconciled rather than summed twice, and the count the reader sees is the reconciled one.
duplicated.never: A duplicate is never added into a total on the quiet.
